# Pattern Review: Brackenford Hall

## Input Quality and Limitations

The log covers two events in one month. E1 and E2 are separate instances, with one occurrence each. Both record the exact wording “The projector cuts out.” Neither includes a diagnosis or investigation record, so both causes are unknown.

## Summary

| Candidate | Occurrences | Distinct Instances | Cause Consistency | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Reported projector cut-outs: E1, E2 | 2 | 2 | Unknown; no diagnoses supplied | High that the reported symptom recurs; insufficient evidence of a shared cause |

## Genuine Patterns

The same reported symptom recurs across two distinct events in different rooms. This supports a repeated symptom, but no underlying-cause pattern can be established.

## Misleading Surface Patterns

E1 and E2 use identical wording. Treating that wording as proof of a common fault would be misleading. The log establishes neither shared nor different causes.

## Isolated Signals, Not Yet Patterns

There are no separately diagnosed isolated signals. Each room has one recorded occurrence, which does not establish recurrence within either room.

## Suggested Actions for Human Approval

Investigate both incidents and record how each diagnosis is established. A person should compare the findings, assess their significance and approve any resulting fix or process change. No common fix is justified yet.

## What This Sample Cannot Tell You

The log cannot establish why either projector cut out, whether the causes match, whether equipment was shared between rooms, or whether the issue extends beyond these two events. Although complete for this month, it does not establish a longer-term trend.
